stem.en: A tissue sample has cells spread far apart in a hard, rigid matrix that contains calcium and phosphorus compounds. What is the main job of this tissue?

text.en: Covering and lining the surfaces of the body and of its organs.

feedback.en: No. A covering tissue has closely packed cells and very little matrix. This tissue has the opposite arrangement.

text.en: Giving strength and support, and protecting organs.

feedback.en: Yes. A hard matrix with calcium and phosphorus belongs to bone, which gives strength, support and protection.

text.en: Carrying messages quickly between parts of the body that are far apart.

feedback.en: No. Messages are carried by neurons, which have long fibres called axons, not a hard matrix.

text.en: Storing food for the body to use later.

feedback.en: No. A hard matrix with calcium and phosphorus gives strength and support; it is not a store of energy.

explanation.en: In a connective tissue, the matrix tells you what the tissue does. A hard, rigid matrix with calcium and phosphorus compounds is found in bone, and bone gives strength, support and protection. A covering tissue has closely packed cells, and neurons have long fibres.

hints.en: In connective tissue, look at the matrix first.
What would a matrix of calcium and phosphorus compounds feel like?
